title: fix: rehearse legacy exec approval conflicts before update activation
body:
Related: #153401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes update rehearsal omitting legacy exec-approval conflicts or misreporting already-imported approval files before activation.

## User Impact

Operators can rehearse legacy approval inputs against private candidate state while preserving the serving policy and original files.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing snapshot owner copies bounded legacy approval bytes with exclusive creation and link rejection, then rebases the matching migration receipt only in the private database. Doctor remains the policy and migration owner. The integration preserves main’s isolated-process SQLite acquisition, cleanup lifecycle, and plugin-code snapshot handling.

## Evidence

Validation on the candidate integrated with fixed main `5050eb796c4ec58f301cf20fd5269e506a257c8d`:

- 104 tests passed across the registered snapshot-worker and exec-approval migration suites. The unchanged four regression cases cover ordinary and interrupted claims, retained receipt authority, and normalized cleanup. Previously captured causal controls fail against the unmodified snapshot implementation.
- With `--maxWorkers=1`, the three-file run took 586.75 seconds wall time (569.24 seconds reported by Vitest), including a 147.06-second cold worker build. The four regression test bodies took 31.16 seconds combined.
- Full changed-code checks passed, including the core and all 25 core-test type graphs, formatting, lint, policy guards, runtime import-cycle checks, and unused-export scans.
- Managed independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

Maintainer scope decision: accept this repair for an installed updater containing the new projection. It cannot retroactively change the snapshot worker selected by the published 2026.9.4 driver. Older-driver recovery remains tracked in #153401.

A fresh published-driver compatibility cell exercised registry `openclaw@2026.9.4` (build `3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107`) against the exact `7eb9f1b1929ec97017c556e1c43ecb00d8263a7d` candidate package. In an isolated Linux arm64 container with Node 24.19.0, the real installed `openclaw update --tag file:<candidate.tgz> --yes --no-restart --json` completed candidate migration rehearsal, Doctor lint, config validation, plugin resolution, continuation checks, and Gateway canary successfully, then swapped the candidate into place. Activation Doctor correctly refused the conflicting legacy exec-approval input. The updater exited 1 with `state-migrated-no-rollback` and `serviceRestartSafe=false`; this is a reproduced older-driver limitation, **not a successful upgrade**. Immediate read-only verification found the canonical `deny` policy (including its stored bytes and timestamp) and the 124-byte conflicting legacy file unchanged. The candidate build remained installed, and the disposable container was removed after evidence capture.

The canonical package build and tarball checks passed; the artifact SHA-256 is `2e5d112f5654491039e2d37794c2a7e6ca749fc4af809d8687c34ca22b0cfc03`. [Exact-head CI also passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36052249073). The 104 registered-worker/Doctor tests above provide the positive proof for an updater containing this change. An earlier isolated macOS attempt stopped before rehearsal because the old driver rejected unrelated legacy records in the host-wide handoff store; that attempt is retained separately and is not counted as successful coverage.

Original contribution by Dallin Romney (@RomneyDa).
